answer: Forging 343 aliases therefore costs 282 bonds held for 21 days each, plus the basalt attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a haven, before it can post or attest. A single raven checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
